marble.name: Plant Cells vs Animal Cells
marble.subject: Science
marble.description: Compare plant and animal cells, identifying shared features and structures unique to plant cells (cell wall, vacuole, chloroplasts)
marble.prompt: If you was shown unlabelled diagrams of a plant cell and an animal cell side by side, could they spot which features are shared and which ones only appear in plant cells — and say why?

cluster.summary: Your child is learning about the amazing diversity of life — identifying different animals and plants, understanding how body parts help animals survive, and discovering what all living things need to stay alive.

misconceptions: Thinking plant cells have a wall INSTEAD of a membrane — plant cells have both; the wall is an extra layer outside the membrane.
Believing every plant cell is green and packed with chloroplasts — many plant cells (roots, stems inside) have few or none.
Assuming animal cells must have some unique organelle to 'balance' the comparison — at this level animal cells share all their parts with plant cells.
Confusing the large permanent vacuole of plant cells with the small temporary vacuoles animal cells can have — treating them as identical.
Over-generalising 'plants are stiff because of the wall' to mean the wall alone — rigidity comes from the wall PLUS a full vacuole creating turgor.
representations: Side-by-side labelled diagrams of a generalised plant cell and animal cell
Venn diagram / two-column sort: shared features vs plant-only features
A 'why does the plant need this?' column linking each unique part to plant lifestyle (photosynthesis, support)
Real onion-epidermis vs cheek-cell microscope images showing the actual presence/absence of wall and chloroplasts
authoredAnswer: Not every plant cell has chloroplasts. Root cells are underground with no light, so they have none and aren't green. Shared by both plant and animal cells: cell membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus and mitochondria. Only in plant cells: the cellulose cell wall, a permanent vacuole, and chloroplasts (in the parts exposed to light).

wrongAnswers.wrong: Every plant cell has chloroplasts, even the root cells underground.
wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Claims root cells photosynthesise or contain chloroplasts
wrongAnswers.fix: Chloroplasts occur only where there is light (leaves, green stems); root cells have none. Contrast a leaf cell with a root hair cell.

wrongAnswers.wrong: Plant cells have a cell wall instead of a cell membrane.
wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Leaves the membrane out of a plant cell because it has a wall
wrongAnswers.fix: Plant cells have BOTH: a cell membrane just inside the rigid cell wall. Label both on a diagram.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Adds plant-only structures to an animal cell
wrongAnswers.fix: Animals don't photosynthesise (no chloroplasts) and have no cellulose wall; only a flexible membrane. Sort structures into a Venn diagram.
